canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_1 = (q, J_1, J_2, beta, T_ov, T_lad, U_{q^2}, T_2, lambda, f) ∈ O_P
canonical_goal.target_object: An exact analytic thermodynamic solution of the one-dimensional J_1-J_2 q-state Potts chain for every integer q >= 2: given real J_1,J_2 and beta > 0, determine the positive number lambda that fixes lim_{N→∞}(1/(2N)) ln Z_{2N} = ln(lambda), where Z_{2N}=Tr exp(-beta H), and f = -beta^{-1} ln(lambda) for H = -J_1 sum_{i=1}^{2N} delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1}) - J_2 sum_{i=1}^{2N} delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+2}), sigma_i ∈ {1,...,q}, sigma_{2N+1}=sigma_1, sigma_{2N+2}=sigma_2. With x = exp(beta J_2), y = exp(beta J_1/2), u = x y^2, v = x + q - 2, and w = sqrt(q-1)y, the target closed form is lambda = (u+v)/2 + sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2 + w^2).
feasibility_constraints: q is an integer with q >= 2; N is a positive integer; beta > 0; J_1 and J_2 are real numbers; each spin variable sigma_i belongs to {1,...,q}; delta(a,b)=1 if a=b and delta(a,b)=0 if a!=b.
The finite chain contains 2N spins with periodic boundary conditions sigma_{2N+1}=sigma_1 and sigma_{2N+2}=sigma_2; the finite-chain partition function is Z_{2N}=Tr exp(-beta H).

The overlapping-pairs transfer matrix T_ov is indexed by ordered pairs (a,b),(a_prime,b_prime) ∈ {1,...,q}^2 and has entries T_ov((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime)) = 1_{b=a_prime} exp((beta J_1/2)(delta(a,b)+delta(a_prime,b_prime)) + beta J_2 delta(a,b_prime)); because the factor 1_{b=a_prime} can be zero, dominance of T_ov is interpreted through lim_{N→∞}(1/(2N))ln Tr(T_ov^{2N}).

The zigzag-ladder transfer matrix T_lad is indexed by ordered pairs (a,b),(a_prime,b_prime) ∈ {1,...,q}^2 and has entries T_lad((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime)) = exp((beta J_1/2)(delta(a,b)+delta(a_prime,b_prime)) + beta J_1 delta(b,a_prime) + beta J_2(delta(a,a_prime)+delta(b,b_prime))); every entry of T_lad is strictly positive and T_lad = T_ov^2, so its unique strictly positive dominant eigenvalue fixes the squared growth factor lambda^2 of T_ov^{2N}.

For any finite real square matrix A with all entries A_{ij}>0, there is exactly one eigenvalue rho(A)>0 whose modulus is strictly larger than every other eigenvalue modulus, and its eigenspace contains a vector with all components strictly positive; if every permutation of the q spin labels commutes with A, this positive eigenvector is unchanged by every such permutation and therefore lies in the span of orbit-sum vectors over the equality classes s=s_prime and s!=s_prime.

The thermodynamic free energy per spin is defined by f = -beta^{-1} lim_{N→∞}(1/(2N)) ln Z_{2N}; the exact-solution claim is feasible only when this limit equals -beta^{-1} ln(lambda) with lambda given by the closed form in the target object.

success_set.definition: Sigma_{P,1} = { o_1 : q ∈ Z, q >= 2, beta > 0, J_1,J_2 ∈ R, delta(a,b)=1 if a=b and delta(a,b)=0 if a!=b, x = exp(beta J_2), y = exp(beta J_1/2), u = x y^2, v = x + q - 2, w = sqrt(q-1)y, T_ov((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime)) = 1_{b=a_prime} exp((beta J_1/2)(delta(a,b)+delta(a_prime,b_prime)) + beta J_2 delta(a,b_prime)) for (a,b),(a_prime,b_prime) ∈ {1,...,q}^2, T_lad((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime)) = exp((beta J_1/2)(delta(a,b)+delta(a_prime,b_prime)) + beta J_1 delta(b,a_prime) + beta J_2(delta(a,a_prime)+delta(b,b_prime))), |psi_1> = q^{-1/2} sum_{s=1}^{q}|s,s>, |psi_2> = (q^2-q)^{-1/2} sum_{s=1}^{q} sum_{s_prime=1}^{q}(1-delta(s,s_prime))|s,s_prime>, U_{q^2}=[|psi_1>,|psi_2>], U_{q^2}^T T_ov U_{q^2} = [[x y^2, sqrt(q-1)y],[sqrt(q-1)y, x+q-2]], U_{q^2}^T T_lad U_{q^2} = (U_{q^2}^T T_ov U_{q^2})^2, lambda = (u+v)/2 + sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2 + w^2), H = -J_1 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1}) - J_2 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+2}), sigma_i ∈ {1,...,q}, sigma_{2N+1}=sigma_1, sigma_{2N+2}=sigma_2, Z_{2N}=Tr exp(-beta H), lim_{N→∞}(1/(2N)) ln Z_{2N} = ln(lambda), and f = -beta^{-1} ln(lambda) }

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily is the full indexing set { (q,J_1,J_2,beta) : q ∈ Z, q >= 2, J_1 ∈ R, J_2 ∈ R, beta > 0 }; for each member, x = exp(beta J_2), y = exp(beta J_1/2), u = x y^2, v = x+q-2, w=sqrt(q-1)y, and lambda=(u+v)/2+sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2+w^2) is asserted to satisfy lim_{N→∞}(1/(2N))ln Tr(T_ov^{2N})=ln(lambda) and f=-beta^{-1}ln(lambda).

canonical_goal.target_object: An exact mapping at the level of the dominant transfer block, dominant eigenvalue, and thermodynamic free energy from the one-dimensional J_1-J_2 q-state Potts chain H = -J_1 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1}) - J_2 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+2}) to the simpler one-dimensional q-state field Potts chain H_eff = -J_2 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1}) - J_1 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,1), for every q ∈ Z with q >= 2, beta > 0, and J_1,J_2 ∈ R.
feasibility_constraints: The source model is H = -J_1 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1}) - J_2 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+2}) with sigma_i ∈ {1,...,q}, q ∈ Z, q >= 2, beta > 0, J_1,J_2 ∈ R, sigma_{2N+1}=sigma_1, and sigma_{2N+2}=sigma_2.

The target model is H_eff = -J_2 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1}) - J_1 sum_{i=1}^{2N}delta(sigma_i,1) with the same q, beta, J_1, J_2, spin alphabet, and periodic one-dimensional chain length.

The q x q transfer matrix for H_eff is T_q(a,b)=exp(beta J_2 delta(a,b)+(beta J_1/2)(delta(a,1)+delta(b,1))) for a,b ∈ {1,...,q}; with x=exp(beta J_2) and y=exp(beta J_1/2), this is T_q(a,b)=x^{delta(a,b)}y^{delta(a,1)+delta(b,1)} and every entry is strictly positive.

The two q x 1 vectors |phi_1>=sum_{s=1}^{q}delta(s,1)|s> and |phi_2>=(q-1)^{-1/2}sum_{s=1}^{q}(1-delta(s,1))|s> are well-defined for q >= 2 and span the two orbit-sum directions formed by the singleton state 1 and the q-1 states not equal to 1.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_3 = (q, J_1, E_0, C_1, C_2, S_0, phase_label, Delta_0, Delta_2) ∈ O_P
canonical_goal.target_object: An exact zero-temperature characterization of the frustrated one-dimensional J_1-J_2 q-state Potts chain after setting J_2=-1, together with the residual-entropy comparison used to explain the finite-temperature dome-like entropy morphology: determine, for q=2 and for every integer q>=3, the J_1 intervals, critical points, nearest-neighbor correlation C_1=<delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1})>, next-nearest-neighbor correlation C_2=<delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+2})>, ground-state energy per spin E_0=-J_1 C_1 + C_2, residual entropy per spin S_0 in the beta→∞ limit, and for q>=3 the entropy gaps Delta_0(q)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2) and Delta_2(q)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1), whose limits Delta_0(q)→0 and Delta_2(q)→0 as q→∞ encode the large-q disappearance of the critical-point entropy excess.
feasibility_constraints: The phase-characterization outcome is restricted to the frustrated normalization J_2=-1, so -J_2=1 is the energy unit and J_1 is dimensionless in that unit; q is an integer with q>=2; beta>0; zero temperature is the asymptotic substitution beta→∞ applied to lambda=(u+v)/2+sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2+w^2).

With J_2=-1, x=exp(-beta), y=exp(beta J_1/2), u=xy^2=exp(beta(J_1-1)), v=x+q-2=exp(-beta)+q-2, and w=sqrt(q-1)y=sqrt(q-1)exp(beta J_1/2); the beta→∞ branch is obtained by comparing the exponential rates J_1-1, 0, and J_1/2 for u, v, and w when q>=3, with q=2 handled separately because v=exp(-beta).
The correlations are defined by C_1 = -∂f/∂J_1 and C_2 = -∂f/∂J_2 before substituting J_2=-1; the ground-state energy per spin after substituting J_2=-1 is E_0 = -J_1 C_1 + C_2.

The residual entropy per spin is S_0 = lim_{beta→∞} S(beta), where S(beta) = -∂f/∂T_abs and beta=1/(k_B T_abs); if a phase has A allowed continuations per spin, then S_0=ln(A), and if a phase has A allowed continuations per two spins, then S_0=(1/2)ln(A).

For the residual-entropy mechanism when q>=3, define Delta_0(q)=S_0(J_1=0)-S_0(J_1<0)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2) and Delta_2(q)=S_0(J_1=2)-S_0(0<J_1<2)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1); the large-q statement is the pair of limits lim_{q→∞}Delta_0(q)=0 and lim_{q→∞}Delta_2(q)=0.

success_set.definition: Sigma_{P,3} = { o_3 : J_2=-1 and the following statements hold. For q=2: if J_1<-2 then phase_label='antiferromagnetic', C_1=0, C_2=1, E_0=1, S_0=0; if -2<J_1<2 then phase_label='dimerized', C_1=1/2, C_2=0, E_0=-J_1/2, S_0=0; if J_1>2 then phase_label='ferromagnetic', C_1=1, C_2=1, E_0=-J_1+1, S_0=0; at J_1=-2 and J_1=2, S_0=ln((1+sqrt(5))/2). For every integer q>=3: if J_1<0 then phase_label='paramagnet with sigma_i different from sigma_{i-1} and sigma_{i-2}', C_1=0, C_2=0, E_0=0, S_0=ln(q-2); at J_1=0, S_0=ln(q-1); if 0<J_1<2 then phase_label='randomly dimerized state with neighboring equal pairs and consecutive pairs different', C_1=1/2, C_2=0, E_0=-J_1/2, S_0=(1/2)ln(q-1); at J_1=2, S_0=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2); if J_1>2 then phase_label='ferromagnetic mixture of q uniform states', C_1=1, C_2=1, E_0=-J_1+1, S_0=0. For every integer q>=3, Delta_0(q)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2)>0 and Delta_2(q)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1)>0; moreover lim_{q→∞}Delta_0(q)=0 and lim_{q→∞}Delta_2(q)=0. The finite-temperature dome statement is encoded only as this residual-entropy mechanism: finite q has positive critical-point entropy excess over the adjacent lower-entropy branch, while the large-q limits remove that excess. }

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated formal goal is the joint conjunction of three propositions. Proposition 1: for every q ∈ Z with q>=2, beta>0, and J_1,J_2 ∈ R, the one-dimensional J_1-J_2 q-state Potts chain has lambda=(u+v)/2+sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2+w^2), where u=exp(beta J_2)exp(beta J_1), v=exp(beta J_2)+q-2, w=sqrt(q-1)exp(beta J_1/2), and f=-beta^{-1}ln(lambda). Proposition 2: the same 2 x 2 block [[exp(beta J_2)exp(beta J_1),sqrt(q-1)exp(beta J_1/2)],[sqrt(q-1)exp(beta J_1/2),exp(beta J_2)+q-2]] is obtained from H_eff=-J_2 sum_i delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1})-J_1 sum_i delta(sigma_i,1), so the source and target models share lambda and f. Proposition 3: after setting J_2=-1 and applying beta→∞, the q=2 chain has phases separated at J_1=-2 and J_1=2, while every q>=3 chain has phases separated at J_1=0 and J_1=2; the corresponding residual entropies are S_0=ln((1+sqrt(5))/2) at the q=2 critical points, S_0=ln(q-1) at J_1=0 for q>=3, S_0=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2) at J_1=2 for q>=3, S_0=ln(q-2) in the q>=3,J_1<0 phase, S_0=(1/2)ln(q-1) in the q>=3,0<J_1<2 phase, and S_0=0 in the noncritical q=2 phases and in the q>=3,J_1>2 phase; for q>=3, the entropy gaps Delta_0(q)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2) and Delta_2(q)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1) are positive for finite q and both vanish as q→∞.

operational_goal.formalisation: The operational goal is achieved by three symbolic checks. Check 1: define T_ov((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime))=1_{b=a_prime}exp((beta J_1/2)(delta(a,b)+delta(a_prime,b_prime))+beta J_2 delta(a,b_prime)), T_lad((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime))=exp((beta J_1/2)(delta(a,b)+delta(a_prime,b_prime))+beta J_1 delta(b,a_prime)+beta J_2(delta(a,a_prime)+delta(b,b_prime))), |psi_1>=q^{-1/2}sum_{s=1}^{q}|s,s>, |psi_2>=(q^2-q)^{-1/2}sum_{s=1}^{q}sum_{s_prime=1}^{q}(1-delta(s,s_prime))|s,s_prime>, U_{q^2}=[|psi_1>,|psi_2>], compute U_{q^2}^T T_ov U_{q^2}=[[xy^2,sqrt(q-1)y],[sqrt(q-1)y,x+q-2]], and set lambda to the larger eigenvalue of this 2 x 2 matrix, lambda=(u+v)/2+sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2+w^2). Check 2: define T_q(a,b)=exp(beta J_2 delta(a,b)+(beta J_1/2)(delta(a,1)+delta(b,1))) and V_q=[sum_{s=1}^{q}delta(s,1)|s>, (q-1)^{-1/2}sum_{s=1}^{q}(1-delta(s,1))|s>], and verify V_q^T T_q V_q=[[xy^2,sqrt(q-1)y],[sqrt(q-1)y,x+q-2]]. Check 3: substitute J_2=-1 into lambda, apply beta→∞ by comparing u=exp(beta(J_1-1)), v=exp(-beta)+q-2, and w=sqrt(q-1)exp(beta J_1/2), and recover the phase labels, C_1, C_2, E_0, and S_0 defined by the following cases: q=2 has critical points J_1=-2 and J_1=2 with S_0=ln((1+sqrt(5))/2), antiferromagnetic C_1=0,C_2=1 for J_1<-2, dimerized C_1=1/2,C_2=0 for -2<J_1<2, and ferromagnetic C_1=1,C_2=1 for J_1>2; q>=3 has critical points J_1=0 with S_0=ln(q-1) and J_1=2 with S_0=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2), paramagnetic C_1=0,C_2=0 for J_1<0, randomly dimerized C_1=1/2,C_2=0 for 0<J_1<2, and ferromagnetic C_1=1,C_2=1 for J_1>2. Check 4: for integer q>=3, compute Delta_0(q)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2) and Delta_2(q)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1), verify both are positive for finite q, and verify lim_{q→∞}Delta_0(q)=lim_{q→∞}Delta_2(q)=0.

implicit_goal.formalisation: The best-fitting implicit canonical goal is the joint conjunction of these three self-contained propositions: (1) for every q>=2 and real J_1,J_2 at beta>0, H=-J_1 sum_i delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1})-J_2 sum_i delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+2}) has thermodynamic free energy f=-beta^{-1}ln(lambda), lambda=(u+v)/2+sqrt(((u-v)/2)^2+w^2), u=exp(beta J_2)exp(beta J_1), v=exp(beta J_2)+q-2, w=sqrt(q-1)exp(beta J_1/2); (2) for the same parameters, H_eff=-J_2 sum_i delta(sigma_i,sigma_{i+1})-J_1 sum_i delta(sigma_i,1) yields the same dominant 2 x 2 transfer block and hence the same lambda and f; (3) for J_2=-1 and beta→∞, q=2 has critical points J_1=-2 and J_1=2, q>=3 has critical points J_1=0 and J_1=2, and the phase correlations, energies, and residual entropies are those obtained by differentiating f and taking the beta→∞ asymptotic branches stated in the phase-characterisation success predicate; additionally, for integer q>=3, Delta_0(q)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2)>0 and Delta_2(q)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1)>0 with both gaps tending to 0 as q→∞.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The operational artefacts instantiate the mathematical targets: a closed-form lambda and f for the source chain, equality of the source and field-Potts projected transfer blocks, and zero-temperature phase/residual-entropy characterization derived from f=-beta^{-1}ln(lambda). The residual-entropy-gap comparison Delta_0(q)=ln(q-1)-ln(q-2) and Delta_2(q)=ln((1+sqrt(4q-3))/2)-(1/2)ln(q-1) captures the paper's finite-temperature dome explanation without overclaiming exact finite-temperature phase-boundary formulae. The stated channel also includes AI-bootstrapping, material-application, table-tennis/time-series, and broad field-building claims. AI bootstrapping is represented as a methodological_claim, while the application and field-building phrases are recorded in excluded_aims; therefore the mathematical channels align with each other but diverge from the rhetorical framing, so consistency_relation is framing_divergence rather than aligned.
